ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, fold $\triangle ABC$ along its median $DE$, with point $A$ landing on point $F$. If $\angle C = 120^\circ$ and $\angle A = 20^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle FEB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle C=120^\circ$ and $\angle A=20^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle B=40^\circ$,\\
since DE is the median line of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it implies that DE$\parallel$BC,\\
thus, $\angle B+\angle DEB=180^\circ$, and $\angle B=\angle AED=\angle DEF=40^\circ$\\
which leads to $\angle DEB=140^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle FEB=\angle DEB-\angle DEF=\boxed{100^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the bottom side is A-E-B collinear, A is on the left side, B is on the right side, and E is located on AB; C is in the upper right, D is at a position near the left middle and is connected with E to form the crease DE; dashed lines connect from A to D and E, indicating the position before folding; after folding, point A lands at F above, and there are line segments DF and EF in the figure; what is required is ∠FEB. Reasoning: It is known that ∠C=120°, ∠A=20°, so the third angle of triangle ABC is ∠B=180°−120°−20°=40°. According to the problem statement and the figure, DE is the midline of triangle ABC, therefore DE ∥ BC. Since EB and AB are on the same straight line, and ED ∥ BC, ∠DEB and ∠B are supplementary, obtaining ∠DEB=180°−40°=140°. Also because EA and BA are on the same straight line and ED ∥ BC, ∠AED=∠B=40°. When folding along DE, ray EA is reflected about the crease DE to ray EF, therefore ∠DEF=∠AED=40°. Thus ∠FEB=∠DEB−∠DEF=140°−40°=100°.
